open_questions: No further open question; scattered depths, sector inconsistency and odd/even preference already favour non-planet
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 2.9 Earth-radius dip every 11.9 days, but the depth jumps from ~1200 ppm in one sector to ~3400 ppm in the next and the five individual transits have strongly inconsistent depths, with one almost missing and one much deeper. Alternate transits are also noticeably different from each other and the centroid is inconclusive while nearby stars can mimic the dip. Together this best matches a background blended eclipse or systematic artefact rather than a planet on the target M dwarf.

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor ~2.6 between sectors. Alone this can be aperture калибration, but sector_depths_by_source confirms changes_within_a_source (p_constant_all 1.8731234057029692e-06) with only QLP sector 3444 ppm vs TESS-SPOC sector 1197 ppm.
reasons.value: p_constant 0.000001851 depth_change_pct 96.83 sector 55 depth_ppm 1197 vs sector 82 depth_ppm 3444

reasons.why: With 5 transits the top 3 carry 94.9% of the signal; one transit is strongly shallow (missing) and one is much deeper. This scatter is at 4.8 sigma and 4.0 sigma from the mean, indicating the dip is not the constant-depth transit required for a planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 3.389587881787827e-12 chi2 59.678192013239034 dof 4 share_of_top_3 0.949 outliers BTJD 2820.81 depth 336 ppm sigma -4.8 and BTJD 3533.472 depth 4641 ppm sigma 4.0

reasons.why: Alternate transits differ at 3.55 sigma (strong threshold 4, but ratio 1.8 with opposite sectors) consistently for odd vs even (sector_oe_same_sign_share 1). Favours binary folded at twice period rather than consistent planet transit.

No on-target centroid to prove dip is on star, while 2 stars inside 1 TESS pixel can plausibly cause dip with ~18-11% eclipse, supporting blended-binary/neighbour contamination over a clean planet. xgboost planet_rank 0.2 also ranks this as planet-unlike.
